App._comment: PublicBaseUrl = the externally reachable HTTPS origin of this app (no trailing slash). Telegram webhooks are registered as {PublicBaseUrl}/api/integrations/telegram/webhook/{connectionId}. Required for local testing (use an https tunnel URL); on Render set App__PublicBaseUrl. If empty, the current request's host is used unless it is localhost.

WhatsApp._comment: Global switch for which provider carries WhatsApp: 'meta' (Cloud API directly, Embedded Signup) or 'infobip' (SculptFlow's Infobip account, MVP). Set WhatsApp__Provider=infobip on Render. A clinic's connection only works while its own provider is the active one.

Infobip._comment: SculptFlow's single Infobip account, used when WhatsApp:Provider = infobip (see Integrations/Infobip). BaseUrl is the account's personal API base URL from the Infobip portal (e.g. xxxxx.api.infobip.com); ApiKey needs the WhatsApp scopes. Both are secrets-by-convention: set them as the Infobip__BaseUrl / Infobip__ApiKey env vars (or user-secrets), never here. Each clinic only stores its own sender number. TimeoutSeconds and MaxSendAttempts are settings now (section Infobip, docs/configuration.md). WebhookToken = secret for the account-level webhook {App:PublicBaseUrl}/api/integrations/whatsapp/account/events?token=... (template status updates); set via Infobip__WebhookToken; empty = that endpoint is off.

GoogleCalendar._comment: Calendar Integrations (Settings -> Calendar Integrations): SculptFlow's own OAuth2 client for Google Calendar (see Services/GoogleCalendarProviderClient.cs). Create in Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> + Create Credentials -> OAuth client ID, type 'Web application', with an Authorized redirect URI of {App:PublicBaseUrl}/calendar-oauth/google/callback; also enable the Google Calendar API for the project. ClientId is not secret and can stay here; ClientSecret must be set via `dotnet user-secrets set "GoogleCalendar:ClientSecret" "..."` locally or the GoogleCalendar__ClientSecret env var on Render.

GoogleLogin._comment: 'Continue with Google' on the Sign in / Register pages (SculptFlow's own login — separate from GoogleCalendar above, which connects a clinic's calendar). A Web OAuth client in Google Cloud Console -> Google Auth Platform -> Clients, with Authorized redirect URIs {App:PublicBaseUrl}/signin-google and https://localhost:7276/signin-google. Only asks for openid/email/profile. ClientId is not secret and can stay here; ClientSecret must be set via `dotnet user-secrets set "GoogleLogin:ClientSecret" "..."` locally or the GoogleLogin__ClientSecret env var on Render. If either value is empty the button simply isn't shown.

MicrosoftCalendar._comment: Calendar Integrations (Settings -> Calendar Integrations): SculptFlow's own OAuth2 client for Outlook/Microsoft 365 calendars (see Services/OutlookCalendarProviderClient.cs). Register in Azure Portal -> Microsoft Entra ID -> App registrations -> New registration, platform 'Web', with a redirect URI of {App:PublicBaseUrl}/calendar-oauth/outlook/callback; grant it the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions Calendars.ReadWrite, User.Read and offline_access, then create a client secret under Certificates & secrets. ClientId/TenantId are not secret and can stay here; ClientSecret must be set via user-secrets or the MicrosoftCalendar__ClientSecret env var on Render. TenantId can stay 'common' (work/school + personal Microsoft accounts) or be a specific tenant id to restrict to one organization.

TikTok._comment: TikTok Login Kit (Settings -> Channels & Integrations): SculptFlow's own OAuth2 client for TikTok account connection (see Services/TikTokProviderClient.cs) — account authorization only, not a messaging channel yet. Create/configure in the TikTok Developer Portal (developers.tiktok.com) -> your app -> Login Kit, with a redirect URI of exactly {App:PublicBaseUrl}/tiktok-oauth/callback. TikTok calls these 'Client Key'/'Client Secret'. ClientKey is not secret and can stay here; ClientSecret must be set via `dotnet user-secrets set "TikTok:ClientSecret" "..."` locally or the TikTok__ClientSecret env var on Render. A Sandbox app's Client Key/Secret work identically to a Production app's for this OAuth flow — moving to production just needs the app itself approved and these two values swapped.

N8n._comment: Shared secret n8n must send as the X-Ingest-Key header on POST /api/messages/ingest. Keep the real value out of this file (checked into the repo) — set it via `dotnet user-secrets set "N8n:IngestApiKey" "..."` instead; user-secrets overrides whatever is here.
N8n._comment2: KnowledgeBenchmarkWebhookUrl = the production webhook URL of the SEPARATE n8n workflow that writes patient-style questions for the Knowledge Retrieval Benchmark (Knowledge Base -> Benchmark -> Generate Test Cases). Not the patient AI workflow. Set it via the N8n__KnowledgeBenchmarkWebhookUrl env var / user-secrets; empty disables question generation (cases can still be added by hand).
N8n._comment3: Calendar Integrations (Settings -> Calendar Integrations): SculptFlow owns the Google/Outlook OAuth connection directly now (GoogleCalendar:*/MicrosoftCalendar:* above) — this SEPARATE n8n workflow only executes the appointment create/update/cancel sync call itself, using a SculptFlow-issued access token (see CalendarSyncTriggerPayload), sent only AFTER the SculptFlow appointment change already succeeded. Set via N8n__CalendarSyncWebhookUrl env var or user-secrets; empty leaves connect/disconnect/calendar-picking fully working but appointment sync inert (logged, not an error).

PlatformAdmin._comment: Platform-admin API (/api/platform-admin/{domain}/*, e.g. billing), called server to server by the SculptFlowAdmin portal. ApiKey is a SECRET sent as X-Platform-Admin-Key — set it via the PlatformAdmin__ApiKey env var or user-secrets, never here, and give the portal the same value (MainApp__PlatformAdminApiKey). Empty = every platform-admin endpoint is off (404).
